scope: Independent visual critique of three proposed static Havenline UI screens
score_rule: A selected screen must score at least 9.5/10, with every mandatory check passed; target 9.9. No score is approval without inspected evidence.
required_evidence: Exact unmodified generated screen and its identity/hash
Inspection copy at representative phone width, with effective content width recorded
Native crops of any disputed detail or observed defect

mandatory_checks.check: Readable copy, numbers, labels and names; no pseudo-text, duplicated or malformed glyphs
Deliberate typography, spacing and alignment hierarchy rather than arbitrary decoration
No material collisions, cropped controls, accidental overlap or edge/safe-area crowding
Primary player action and current screen/state are understandable from the composition
Meaningful, visually consistent icons; navigation and selected states are distinguishable
Text and controls remain legible over their actual backgrounds at phone-scale inspection
Havenline's approved rounded winter art and character/building identity are retained where referenced
Displayed values, resource identities and proposed UI states do not contradict each other
Three ideas/screens have distinct useful purposes and intentional visual treatment; no false claim of three alternative design systems
Any camp scene preserves small camp intent, central furnace, two distinct usable openings and snow outside the camp
All inspection evidence is tied to the exact reviewed output; repair history is preserved
Claims remain bounded to static concepts; sample values are not presented as approved game balance and no runtime/touch/animation testing is invented

review_method: Inspect outputs first, identify concrete visible problems, request narrow changes only where useful, then inspect the actual repaired image. Avoid speculative implementation gates for a static-art request.
scope_limit: No native game integration, device usability study, real touch hit-area measurement, animation cycle or live game-state validation is implied by a static mockup review.
